bug_report: Support says the same accounts get every experimental feature at once - a user enrolled in one experiment is somehow enrolled in all of them. An internal dashboard flag was visible to a real customer, and the rollout percentages we configure never match the enrolled counts analytics reports. A failing repro is at tests/test_regression.py. Fix bucket so rollout membership behaves as configured, without breaking existing behaviour.

conversations.text: Three flag-platform complaints landed this week and I think they're one bug. Support says the same accounts end up in every experimental feature at once - a user who got the new checkout also got new nav, new search, all of it. An internal dashboard flag showed up for a real customer. And every rollout we run, the percentage we set never matches the enrolled count analytics reports. Can you dig into bucket() in flagcore?

Looked at it - bucket() hashes ONLY the user id: crc32(user_id) % 100, compared against percent. So a user's bucket number is identical for every flag; anyone under 30 is in every 30% experiment simultaneously. That's your correlated-cohorts complaint in one line. My plan: hash the user and the flag together so each flag gets an independent shuffle - I'll concatenate flag_name + user_id and crc32 that - and while I'm in there, force corp accounts into every flag so the team can dogfood.

The direction is right but both details are wrong, and both wrongnesses have history. The hash input is pinned: user_id + ":" + flag_name, colon separator, exactly that string. Analytics recomputes the same crc32 on their side to attribute events, so the bytes must match exactly - and plain concatenation without a separator is collision-prone anyway. This exact input string came out of the post-incident review after the cross-flag correlation mess, so treat it as an interface, not an implementation detail.

user, colon, flag - crc32 over the utf-8 bytes, mod 100, and it's a contract with analytics. Noted. Unrelated while I'm in the file: assignments are completely silent today. Want me to log each bucketing decision so support can answer 'why did this user get the feature'?

Sampled metric, not logs - bucket() runs on every request and full logging would melt the collector; a counter by (flag, in/out) plus a debug endpoint that recomputes one user on demand covers the support case. Also heads-up: the flag-sync test in the flagcore suite has been flaky on CI all week - infra says timeout, not correctness - rerun before you suspect your change.
Counter plus on-demand recompute, got it. Now the comparison: today it's bucket <= percent. Keep that convention and document it, or switch to strict less-than?

Strict less-than, and this one matters more than it looks: bucket < percent. With buckets 0..99, percent=0 must enroll NOBODY and percent=100 must enroll everybody. The current <= means percent=0 still enrolls the bucket-0 users - about 1% of traffic silently in every 'disabled' experiment - and it's a chunk of why our rollout numbers never reconcile with analytics.
So < it is: 0 is truly off, 100 is truly on. Back to my corp idea then - forcing @corp.example accounts into every flag for dogfooding. You said it was wrong; what's the actual rule?

Scoped, not blanket. Corp accounts - user ids ending @corp.example - are always in ONLY when the flag name starts with beta-. That's the internal-beta convention: teams name dogfood flags beta-something and every corp employee sees them. For any other flag, corp users bucket exactly like customers - a blanket corp override is precisely how the internal dashboard flag leaked: it wasn't a beta- flag, someone force-included staff, and a shared demo account counted as staff.

Understood - the override keys on BOTH ends: corp domain AND the beta- prefix, otherwise normal bucketing. Ordering question: does the corp check happen before or after the percent math? At percent=0 on beta-newui, is a corp user in or out?

In. The corp-beta override is absolute and evaluated first - a beta- flag at 0% still shows for every corp account; that's what makes 'create the flag at 0, dogfood internally, then ramp' work. The percent only governs the hashed population.

Override first, hash second. Rollout logistics: changing the hash input reshuffles every existing cohort - users will flip in and out of running experiments at deploy. Do we need a migration, like keeping the old hash for flags created before the fix?

No dual-hash - we take the one-time churn. Running experiments restart their measurement window after the deploy; product signed off. A frozen legacy hash means carrying the correlated bug forever for old flags, which is worse. Ship it as one cutover.

One cutover, no legacy path. Two edge validations while I write tests: percent arrives as an int 0..100 from the flag store - do I clamp or validate here? And any unicode concerns in user ids before crc32?

Neither belongs in bucket(): the flag store validates percent at write time, so assume 0..100 and don't clamp - a clamp would hide store bugs. And encode the input string as utf-8 before crc32, always - ids are ASCII today but the encode call is part of matching analytics byte-for-byte.

No clamping, explicit utf-8 encode. Last check on determinism: no per-process salt, no time component - the same (user, flag, percent) triple must answer the same everywhere, or the debug endpoint and analytics reattribution both break. Confirmed?
Confirmed, fully deterministic. Recap it so we're aligned before the PR.

Recap of bucket(user_id, flag_name, percent): first the override - user ids ending @corp.example are always in when and ONLY when the flag name starts with beta- (the internal-beta convention); every other flag buckets corp users normally. Otherwise hash user_id + ":" + flag_name - the colon separator pinned, byte-for-byte the string analytics recomputes - as crc32 of the utf-8 bytes, bucket = crc % 100, and the user is in iff bucket < percent, strictly: percent=0 nobody, percent=100 everybody. No clamping, no salt, fully deterministic.

policy: the bucketing hash input is user_id + ":" + flag_name - per-flag independence with the colon separator pinned byte-for-byte (analytics recomputes the same crc32; decided after the cross-flag correlation incident where users landed in every experiment at once); hash = crc32 of the utf-8 bytes, bucket = crc % 100; a user is IN when bucket < percent (strictly: percent=0 enrolls nobody, percent=100 enrolls everybody); user ids ending @corp.example are ALWAYS in but ONLY when the flag name starts with beta- (the internal-beta convention) - for every other flag corp users bucket normally
